messages:
amy-acme: Hi team — after our org's bulk service-account import via Okta SCIM yesterday, a few devs are getting 403 in Console when switching into project 'acme-internal'. API calls show missing scope errors. Repro below.

matt-support: Sorry about that. Can you attach the curl and the exact error body? Also confirm whether keys were created by SCIM provisioning or the API.

amy-acme: Heres the curl we ran: `curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey sk_abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acme-internal/summary -v`
Response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`
Body: `{"error":"permission_denied", "details":"missing scope: project:read"}`
All keys were created by our IdP provisioning job (Okta -> SCIM).

sara-eng: Thanks @amy-acme. Quick debug steps: 1) can support fetch the stored metadata for that key id? 2) did the provisioning payload include scopes as a single string or array? We saw a couple of weird imports where the scopes looked like `projects:read, projects:write` (note comma+space).

matt-support: I pulled the key record (internal id ak_77). Pre-import snapshot: `projects:read,projects:write,org:billing`. Post-import DB value: `projects:read projects:write` (commas removed). The scope parser expects commas; when commas are missing it treats the whole string differently and drops the last token. That explains the 403.

vikas-sre: ops-bot flagged similar failures across multiple orgs. ops-bot: alert created.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-5491. Affected: 7 orgs, ~21 API keys. Severity: P1 (auth regression impacting Console/project switches). Assigned to eng-runtime.

amy-acme: Yikes. Any immediate workaround? Our SREs need a short-term fix as several CI jobs are blocked.

vikas-sre: Workarounds: (A) Regenerate the API keys manually from Console (ensures scopes are set correctly); (B) If you have Dedicated tokens, create a service token which uses the alternate scope path; (C) We can run a DB backfill to reinsert commas for keys created by provisioning in the last 72h — requires platform + legal signoff.

sara-eng: Root cause (quick summary): SCIM sanitizer in provisioning pipeline normalizes whitespace but strips punctuation when input contains comma+space. The sanitizer replaced `, ` with ` ` which removed commas, leading to bad tokenization. Fix is to preserve commas or to canonicalize using explicit split on comma and trim.

matt-support: Ive DM'd PM with list of affected orgs. Will notify customers privately.

pm-jess: Please prepare a short customer note: ask any teams that used SCIM/provisioning to check keys created in last 72h and regenerate if they see 403. We'll coordinate an email once we have the migration timeline.

vikas-sre: Engineering plan: 1) hotfix sanitizer to avoid removing commas (PR opened), 2) backfill script to correct DB entries for recent creations, 3) add schema validation on provisioning to reject malformed scope strings. ETA for hotfix: ~2-4 hours. Backfill ETA after review.

sara-eng: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/provisioning/commit/def456 (hotfix). Backfill tracked in INC-5491.

amy-acme: Thanks everyone, we'll rotate the two blocked keys now and test. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

matt-support: Added monitoring: new alert for any created API key with empty/whitespace-only scopes or scopes without commas. Should prevent silent failures in future.

vikas-sre: We'll post a postmortem once the backfill runs and root cause is confirmed. For now, manual regen or dedicated token is the recommended short-term action.

amy-acme: Confirmed manual regen fixed the engineers' access. Thanks all :heart:
